topic: What beam management strategies are needed to mitigate efficiency fluctuations (>3 dB gain variance) across the 57-66 GHz band?
consensus_response: To mitigate efficiency fluctuations, adaptive beamforming techniques are necessary to adjust beamwidth and directionality in real-time. This compensates for changing channel conditions caused by narrower beams, which limit the effective spread of rays in both angular and time domain. As a result, system capacity will increase due to reduced interference. However, this requires more complex resource allocation algorithms to optimize bandwidth and power distribution among beams, increasing complexity in beam management and scheduling.
reference_context: The reference context highlights the challenges of mmWave bands, including increased path loss and interference due to narrower beams. The maximum achievable gain is limited to 51.8 dBi, and adaptive beamforming techniques are necessary to mitigate these effects.
